Sources and Uses of Liquidity

    We have mulple sources of liquidity to meet our capital needs, including annual cash ﬂows, accumulated earnings in our businesses,
the proceeds from our issuances of senior notes and other borrowings, liquid investments we hold on our Consolidated Statement of
Financial Condion and access to our $4.325 billion commied revolving credit facility (the “Revolving Credit Facility”). As of
December 31, 2025, Blackstone had $2.6 billion in Cash and Cash Equivalents, $359.7 million invested in Corporate Treasury Investments
and $7.1 billion in Other Investments (which included $6.5 billion of liquid investments), against $12.4 billion in borrowings from our
bond issuances. As of December 31, 2025, we had no borrowings outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility. In February 2026, we
drew $900.0 million under the Revolving Credit Facility.

    On November 3, 2025, Blackstone, through its subsidiary Blackstone Reg Finance Co. L.L.C., issued $600 million aggregate principal
amount of 4.300% senior notes due November 3, 2030 (the “Registered 2030 Notes”), and $600 million aggregate principal amount of
4.950% senior notes due February 15, 2036 (the “Registered 2036 Notes” and, together with the Registered 2030 Notes, the “Registered
Notes”), pursuant to a Registraon Statement on Form S-3. Blackstone intends to use the net proceeds from the sale of the Registered
Notes for general corporate purposes. For addional informaon see Note 12. “Borrowings” in the “Notes to Consolidated Financial
Statements” in “—Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data” of this ﬁling and “—Notable Transacons”.

                                                                                                                                       128
     In addion to the cash we receive from our notes oﬀerings and availability under the Revolving Credit Facility and other borrowings,
we expect to receive (a) cash generated from operang acvies, (b) Performance Revenue realizaons, and (c) realizaons on the fund
investments that we make. The amounts and ming of cash received from sources in parcular may vary substanally from year to year
and quarter to quarter depending on the frequency and size of realizaon events, ming of selement, the form in which we elect to
receive payment (including in-kind) and net returns experienced by our investment funds. Our available capital could be adversely
aﬀected if there are prolonged periods of few substanal realizaons from our investment funds accompanied by substanal capital calls
for new investments from those investment funds. Therefore, Blackstone’s commitments to our funds are taken into consideraon when
managing our overall liquidity and cash posion.

     We expect that our primary liquidity needs will be cash to (a) provide capital to facilitate the growth of our exisng businesses, which
includes, without limitaon, funding our general partner and co-investment commitments to our funds and warehousing investments for
our funds, (b) provide capital for business expansion, (c) pay operang expenses, including cash compensaon to our employees, and
other obligaons as they arise, including servicing debts, (d) pay income taxes and (e) pay dividends to our stockholders, make
distribuons to the holders of Blackstone Holdings Partnership Units and make repurchases under our share repurchase program. For a
tabular presentaon of Blackstone’s contractual obligaons and the expected ming of such see “—Contractual Obligaons.”

Crical Accounng Policies

    We prepare our consolidated ﬁnancial statements in accordance with GAAP. In applying many of these accounng principles, we
need to make assumpons, esmates and/or judgments that aﬀect the reported amounts of assets, liabilies, revenues and expenses in
our consolidated ﬁnancial statements. We base our esmates and judgments on historical experience and other assumpons that we
believe are reasonable under the circumstances. These assumpons, esmates and/or judgments, however, are o en subjecve. Actual
results may be aﬀected negavely based on changing circumstances. If actual amounts are ulmately diﬀerent from our esmates, the
revisions are included in our results of operaons for the period in which the actual amounts become known. We believe the following
crical accounng policies could potenally produce materially diﬀerent results if we were to change underlying assumpons, esmates
and/or judgments. For a descripon of our accounng policies, see Note 2. “Summary of Signiﬁcant Accounng Policies” in the “Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements” in “—Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data” of this ﬁling.

Principles of Consolidaon

     For a descripon of our accounng policy on consolidaon, see Note 2. “Summary of Signiﬁcant Accounng Policies—Consolidaon”
and Note 8. “Variable Interest Enes” in the “Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements” in “—Item 8. Financial Statements and
Supplementary Data” for detailed informaon on Blackstone’s involvement with VIEs. The following discussion is intended to provide
supplemental informaon about how the applicaon of consolidaon principles impact our ﬁnancial results, and management’s process
for implemenng those principles including areas of signiﬁcant judgment.

     The determinaon that Blackstone holds a controlling ﬁnancial interest in a Blackstone Fund or investment vehicle signiﬁcantly
changes the presentaon of our consolidated ﬁnancial statements. In our Consolidated Statements of Financial Posion included in this
ﬁling, we present 100% of the assets and liabilies of consolidated VIEs along with a non-controlling interest which represents the poron
of the consolidated vehicle’s interests held by third pares. However, assets of our consolidated VIEs can only be used to sele
obligaons of the consolidated VIE and are not available for general use by Blackstone. Further, the liabilies of our consolidated VIEs do
not have recourse to the general credit of Blackstone. In the Consolidated Statements of Operaons, we eliminate any management fees,
Incenve Fees, or Performance Allocaons received or accrued from consolidated VIEs as they are considered intercompany transacons.
We recognize 100% of the consolidated VIE’s investment income (loss) and allocate the poron of that income (loss) aributable to third-
party ownership to non-controlling interests in arriving at Net Income Aributable to Blackstone Inc.

    The assessment of whether we consolidate a Blackstone Fund or investment vehicle we manage requires the applicaon of signiﬁcant
judgment. These judgments are applied both at the me we become involved with the VIE and on an ongoing basis and include, but are
not limited to:

    •      Determining whether our management fees, Incenve Fees or Performance Allocaons represent variable interests – We
           make judgments as to whether the fees we earn are commensurate with the level of eﬀort required for those fees and at
           market rates. In making this judgment, we consider, among other things, the extent of third-party investment in the enty and
           the terms of any other interests we hold in the VIE.

                                                                                                                                          138
    •     Determining whether kick-out rights are substanve – We make judgments as to whether the third-party investors in a
          partnership enty have the ability to remove the general partner, the investment manager or its equivalent, or to dissolve
          (liquidate) the partnership enty, through a simple majority vote. This includes an evaluaon of whether barriers to exercise
          these rights exist.
    •     Concluding whether Blackstone has an obligaon to absorb losses or the right to receive beneﬁts that could potenally be
          signiﬁcant to the VIE – As there is no explicit threshold in GAAP to deﬁne “potenally signiﬁcant,” management must apply
          judgment and evaluate both quantave and qualitave factors to conclude whether this threshold is met.

    For a descripon of our accounng policy on revenue recognion, see Note 2. “Summary of Signiﬁcant Accounng Policies—Revenue

    Management and Advisory Fees, Net — Blackstone earns base management fees from its customers at a ﬁxed percentage of a

    •     0.35% to 1.50% of commied capital or invested capital during the investment period, invested capital subsequent to the

    Management fee calculaons based on commied capital or invested capital are mechanical in nature and therefore do not require
the use of signiﬁcant esmates or judgments. Management fee calculaons based on net asset value, gross asset value, or investment fair
value depend on the fair value of the underlying investments within the funds. Esmates and assumpons are made when determining
the fair value of the underlying investments within the funds and could vary depending on the valuaon methodology that is used as well
as economic condions. See “—Fair Value” below for further discussion of the judgment required for determining the fair value of the
underlying investments.

    Investment Income (Loss) — Performance Allocaons are made to the general partner based on cumulave fund performance to
date, subject to a preferred return to limited partners. Blackstone has concluded that investments made alongside its limited partners in
a partnership which entle Blackstone to a Performance Allocaon represent equity method investments that are not in the scope of the
GAAP guidance on accounng for revenues from contracts with customers. Blackstone accounts for these arrangements under the equity
method of accounng. Under the equity method, Blackstone’s share of earnings (losses) from equity method investments is determined
using a balance sheet approach referred to as the hypothecal liquidaon at book value (“HLBV”) method. Under the HLBV method, at
the end of each reporng period Blackstone calculates the accrued Performance Allocaons that would be due to Blackstone for each
fund pursuant to the fund agreements as if the fair value of the underlying investments were realized as of such date, irrespecve of
whether such amounts have been realized. Performance Allocaons are subject to clawback to the extent that the Performance
Allocaon received to date exceeds the amount due to Blackstone based on cumulave results.

    The change in the fair value of the investments held by certain Blackstone Funds is a signiﬁcant input into the accrued Performance
Allocaon calculaon and accrual for potenal repayment of previously received Performance Allocaons. Esmates and assumpons are
made when determining the fair value of the underlying investments within the funds. See “—Fair Value” below for further discussion
related to signiﬁcant esmates and assumpons used for determining fair value of the underlying investments.

Fair Value

     Blackstone uses fair value throughout the reporng process. For a descripon of our accounng policies related to valuaon, see
Note 2. “Summary of Signiﬁcant Accounng Policies—Fair Value of Financial Instruments” and “Summary of Signiﬁcant Accounng
Policies—Investments, at Fair Value” in the “Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements” in “—Item 8. Financial Statements and
Supplementary Data” of this ﬁling. The following discussion is intended to provide supplemental informaon about how the applicaon
of fair value principles impact our ﬁnancial results, and management’s process for implemenng those principles including areas of
signiﬁcant judgment.

    The fair value of the investments held by Blackstone Funds is the primary input to the calculaon of certain of our management fees,
Incenve Fees, Performance Allocaons and the related Compensaon we recognize. Generally, Blackstone Funds are accounted for in
accordance with the GAAP guidance on investment companies, and under the American Instute of Cerﬁed Public Accountants Audit
and Accounng Guide, Investment

                                                                                                                                     140
Companies, and reﬂect their investments, including majority-owned and controlled investments, at fair value. In the absence of
observable market prices, we ulize valuaon methodologies applied on a consistent basis and assumpons that we believe market
parcipants would use to determine the fair value of the investments. For investments where lile market acvity exists management’s
determinaon of fair value is based on the best informaon available in the circumstances, which may incorporate management’s own
assumpons and involves a signiﬁcant degree of judgment, and the consideraon of a combinaon of internal and external factors,
including the appropriate risk adjustments for non-performance and liquidity risks.

     Blackstone has also elected the fair value opon for certain instruments it owns directly, including loans and receivables, investments
in private debt securies and other proprietary investments. Blackstone is required to measure certain ﬁnancial instruments at fair value,
including debt instruments, equity securies and freestanding derivaves.

Fair Value of Investments or Instruments that are Publicly Traded

    Securies that are publicly traded and for which a quoted market exists will be valued at the closing price of such securies in the
principal market in which the security trades, or in the absence of a principal market, in the most advantageous market on the valuaon
date. When a quoted price in an acve market exists, no block discounts or control premiums are permied regardless of the size of the
public security held. In some cases, securies will include legal and contractual restricons liming their purchase and sale for a period of
me. A discount to the publicly traded price may be appropriate in instances where a legal restricon is a characterisc of the security,
such as may be required under SEC Rule 144. The amount of the discount, if taken, shall be determined based on the me period that
must pass before the restricted security becomes unrestricted or otherwise available for sale.

Fair Value of Investments or Instruments that are not Publicly Traded

     Investments for which market prices are not observable include private investments in the equity or debt of operang companies or
real estate properes. Our primary methodology for determining the fair values of such investments is generally the income approach
which provides an indicaon of fair value based on the present value of cash ﬂows that a business, security, or property is expected to
generate in the future. The most widely used methodology under the income approach is the discounted cash ﬂow method which
includes signiﬁcant assumpons about the underlying investment’s projected net earnings or cash ﬂows, discount rate, capitalizaon rate
and exit mulple. Our secondary methodology, generally used to corroborate the results of the income approach, is typically the market
approach. The most widely used methodology under the market approach relies upon valuaons for comparable public companies,
transacons, or assets, and includes making judgments about which companies, transacons, or assets are comparable. Depending on
the facts and circumstances associated with the investment, diﬀerent primary and secondary methodologies may be used including
opon value, conngent claims or scenario analysis, yield analysis, projected cash ﬂow through maturity or expiraon, discount to sale,
probability weighted methods or recent round of ﬁnancing.

    In certain cases debt and equity securies are valued on the basis of prices from an orderly transacon between market parcipants
provided by reputable dealers or pricing services. In determining the value of a parcular investment, pricing services may use certain
informaon with respect to transacons in such investments, quotaons from dealers, pricing matrices and market transacons in
comparable investments and various relaonships between investments.

Management Process on Fair Value

    Due to the importance of fair value throughout the consolidated ﬁnancial statements and the signiﬁcant judgment required to be
applied in arriving at those fair values, we have developed a process around valuaon that incorporates several levels of approval and
review from both internal and external sources. Investments held

                                                                                                                                         141
by Blackstone Funds and investment vehicles are valued on at least a quarterly basis by our internal valuaon or asset management
teams, which are independent from our investment teams. For investments held by vehicles managed by more than one business unit,
Blackstone has developed a process designed to facilitate coordinaon and alignment, as appropriate, of the fair value of in-scope
investments across business units.

    For investments valued ulizing the income method and where Blackstone has informaon rights, we generally have a direct line of
communicaon with each of the companies’ and underlying assets’ ﬁnance teams and collect ﬁnancial data used to support projecons
used in a discounted cash ﬂow analysis. The valuaon team then analyzes the data received and updates the valuaon models reﬂecng
any changes in the underlying cash ﬂow projecons, weighted-average cost of capital, exit mulple or capitalizaon rate, and any other
valuaon input relevant to economic condions.

    The results of all valuaons of investments held by Blackstone Funds and investment vehicles are reviewed by the relevant business
unit’s valuaon sub-commiee, which is comprised of key personnel from the business unit, typically the chief investment oﬃcer, chief
operang oﬃcer, chief ﬁnancial oﬃcer, head of ﬁnance, chief compliance oﬃcer (or their respecve equivalents where applicable) and
other senior managing directors in the business or support funcons. To further corroborate results, each business unit also generally
obtains either a posive assurance opinion or a range of value from an independent valuaon party, at least annually for internally
prepared valuaons for investments that have been held by Blackstone Funds and investment vehicles for greater than a year and
quarterly for certain investments. Our ﬁrmwide valuaon commiee, chaired by our Chief Financial Oﬃcer and comprised of senior
members of our businesses and representaves from corporate funcons, including legal and ﬁnance, reviews the valuaon process for
investments held by us and our investment vehicles, including the applicaon of appropriate valuaon standards on a consistent basis.
Each quarter, the valuaon process is also reviewed by the audit commiee of our board of directors, which is comprised of our
non-employee directors.

Income Tax

    For a descripon of our accounng policy on taxes and addional informaon on taxes see Note 2. “Summary of Signiﬁcant
Accounng Policies” and Note 14. “Income Taxes,” in the “Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements” in “—Item 8. Financial Statements
and Supplementary Data” of this ﬁling.

    Our provision for income taxes is comprised of current and deferred taxes. Current income taxes approximate taxes to be paid or
refunded for the current period. Deferred income taxes reﬂect the net tax eﬀects of temporary diﬀerences between the ﬁnancial
reporng and tax bases of assets and liabilies and are measured using the applicable enacted tax rates and laws that will be in eﬀect
when such diﬀerences are expected to reverse.

    Addionally, signiﬁcant judgment is required in esmang the provision for (beneﬁt from) income taxes, current and deferred tax
balances (including any valuaon allowance), accrued interest or penales and uncertain tax posions. In evaluang these judgments, we
consider, among other items, projecons of taxable income (including the character of such income), beginning with historic results and
incorporang assumpons of the amount of future pretax operang income. These assumpons about future taxable income require
signiﬁcant judgment and are consistent with the plans and esmates that Blackstone uses to manage its business. To the extent any
poron of the deferred tax assets are not considered to be more likely than not to be realized, a valuaon allowance is recorded.

    Revisions in esmates and/or actual costs of a tax assessment may ulmately be materially diﬀerent from the recorded accruals and
unrecognized tax beneﬁts, if any.

Basis for Opinions

    Blackstone’s management is responsible for these ﬁnancial statements, for maintaining eﬀecve internal control over ﬁnancial
reporng, and for its assessment of the eﬀecveness of internal control over ﬁnancial reporng, included in the accompanying
management’s report on internal control over ﬁnancial reporng. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these ﬁnancial

    We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the

Deﬁnion and Limitaons of Internal Control over Financial Reporng

    A company’s internal control over ﬁnancial reporng is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of
ﬁnancial reporng and the preparaon of ﬁnancial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounng
principles. A company’s internal control over ﬁnancial reporng includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the
maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reﬂect the transacons and disposions of the assets of the
company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transacons are recorded as necessary to permit preparaon of ﬁnancial statements in
accordance with generally accepted accounng principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in
accordance with authorizaons of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding
prevenon or mely detecon of unauthorized acquision, use, or disposion of the company’s assets that could have a material eﬀect
on the ﬁnancial statements.

                                                                                                                                          148
    Because of its inherent limitaons, internal control over ﬁnancial reporng may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also,
projecons of any evaluaon of eﬀecveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of
changes in condions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.

Crical Audit Maer Descripon

    Blackstone, as a general partner, is entled to an allocaon of income from certain carry fund and open-ended structures
(“Blackstone Funds”) assuming certain investment returns are achieved, referred to as “Performance Allocaons”. Performance
Allocaons are made based on either cumulave fund performance to date, subject to a preferred return to limited partners or based on
fund or vehicle performance over a period of me, subject to a high water mark and preferred return to investors. The change in the fair
value of the underlying investments held by the Blackstone Funds is the signiﬁcant input into this calculaon.

     As the fair value of underlying investments varies between reporng periods, adjustments are made to amounts recorded as Accrued
Performance Allocaons to reﬂect either (a) posive performance resulng in an increase in the Accrued Performance Allocaon or
(b) negave performance that would cause the amount due to the general partner to be less than the amount previously recognized as
revenue, resulng in a negave adjustment to the Accrued Performance Allocaon to the general partner.

    We considered the valuaon of certain investments without readily determinable fair values used in the calculaon of Performance
Allocaons and Accrued Performance Allocaons as a crical audit maer because of the valuaon techniques, assumpons, market
impacts and the degree of subjecvity of certain unobservable inputs used in the valuaon. Auding the fair value of these investments
required a high degree of auditor judgment and increased eﬀort, including the involvement of our internal fair value specialists as
needed, who possess signiﬁcant fair value methodology and modeling experse.

1. Organizaon

     Blackstone Inc., together with its consolidated subsidiaries (“Blackstone” or the “Company”), is the world’s largest alternave asset
manager. Blackstone’s asset management business includes global investment strategies focused on real estate, private equity,
infrastructure, life sciences, growth equity, credit, real assets, secondaries and hedge funds. “Blackstone Funds” refers to the funds and
other vehicles that are managed by Blackstone. Blackstone’s business is organized into four segments: Real Estate, Private Equity, Credit &
Insurance and Mul-Asset Invesng.

    Blackstone Inc. was inially formed as The Blackstone Group L.P., a Delaware limited partnership, on March 12, 2007. Prior to its
conversion on July 1, 2019 to a Delaware corporaon, Blackstone Inc. was managed and operated by Blackstone Group
Management L.L.C., which is wholly owned by Blackstone’s senior managing directors and controlled by one of Blackstone’s founders,
Stephen A. Schwarzman (the “Founder”).

    The acvies of Blackstone are conducted through its holding partnerships: Blackstone Holdings I L.P., Blackstone Holdings AI L.P.,
Blackstone Holdings II L.P., Blackstone Holdings III L.P. and Blackstone Holdings IV L.P. (collecvely, “Blackstone Holdings,” “Blackstone
Holdings Partnerships” or the “Holding Partnerships”). Blackstone, through its wholly owned subsidiaries, is the sole general partner of
each of the Holding Partnerships. Generally, holders of the limited partner interests in the Holding Partnerships may, four mes each year,
exchange their limited partnership interests (“Partnership Units”) for Blackstone common stock, on a one-to-one basis, exchanging one
Partnership Unit from each of the Holding Partnerships for one share of Blackstone common stock.

2. Summary of Signiﬁcant Accounng Policies

Basis of Presentaon

   The accompanying consolidated ﬁnancial statements of Blackstone have been prepared in accordance with accounng principles
generally accepted in the United States of America (“GAAP”).

    The consolidated ﬁnancial statements include the accounts of Blackstone, its wholly owned or majority-owned subsidiaries, the
consolidated enes which are considered to be variable interest enes and for which Blackstone is considered the primary beneﬁciary,
and certain partnerships or similar enes which are not considered variable interest enes but in which the general partner is
determined to have control.

    All intercompany balances and transacons have been eliminated in consolidaon.

Use of Esmates

    The preparaon of the consolidated ﬁnancial statements in accordance with GAAP requires management to make esmates that
aﬀect the amounts reported in the consolidated ﬁnancial statements and accompanying notes. Management believes that esmates
ulized in the preparaon of the consolidated ﬁnancial statements are prudent and reasonable. Such esmates include those used in the
valuaon of investments and ﬁnancial instruments, the measurement of deferred tax balances (including any valuaon allowances) and
the accounng for Goodwill and equity-based compensaon. Actual results could diﬀer from those esmates and such diﬀerences could
be material.

Consolidaon

    Blackstone consolidates all enes that it controls through a majority vong interest or otherwise, including those Blackstone Funds
in which the general partner has a controlling ﬁnancial interest. Blackstone has a controlling ﬁnancial interest in Blackstone Holdings
because the limited partners do not have the right to dissolve the partnerships or have substanve kick-out rights or parcipang rights
that would overcome the control held by Blackstone. Accordingly, Blackstone consolidates Blackstone Holdings and records
non-controlling interests to reﬂect the economic interests of the limited partners of Blackstone Holdings.

    In addion, Blackstone consolidates all variable interest enes (“VIE”) for which it is the primary beneﬁciary. An enterprise is
determined to be the primary beneﬁciary if it holds a controlling ﬁnancial interest. A controlling ﬁnancial interest is deﬁned as (a) the
power to direct the acvies of a VIE that most signiﬁcantly impact the enty’s economic performance and (b) the obligaon to absorb
losses of the enty or the right to receive beneﬁts from the enty that could potenally be signiﬁcant to the VIE. The consolidaon
guidance requires an analysis to determine (a) whether an enty in which Blackstone holds a variable interest is a VIE and (b) whether
Blackstone’s involvement, through holding interests directly or indirectly in the enty or contractually through other variable interests,
would give it a controlling ﬁnancial interest. Performance of that analysis requires the exercise of judgment.

     Blackstone determines whether it is the primary beneﬁciary of a VIE at the me it becomes involved with a variable interest enty
and connuously reconsiders that conclusion. In determining whether Blackstone is the primary beneﬁciary, Blackstone evaluates its
control rights as well as economic interests in the enty held either directly or indirectly by Blackstone. The consolidaon analysis can
generally be performed qualitavely; however, if it is not readily apparent that Blackstone is not the primary beneﬁciary, a quantave
analysis may also be performed. Investments and redempons (either by Blackstone, aﬃliates of Blackstone or third pares) or
amendments to the governing documents of the respecve Blackstone Funds could aﬀect an enty’s status as a VIE or the determinaon
of the primary beneﬁciary. At each reporng date, Blackstone assesses whether it is the primary beneﬁciary and will consolidate or
deconsolidate accordingly.

    Assets of consolidated VIEs that can only be used to sele obligaons of the consolidated VIE and liabilies of a consolidated VIE for
which creditors (or beneﬁcial interest holders) do not have recourse to the general credit of Blackstone are presented in a separate
secon in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condion.

    Blackstone’s other disclosures regarding VIEs are discussed in Note 8. “Variable Interest Enes.”

Revenue Recognion

    Revenues primarily consist of management and advisory fees, incenve fees, investment income, interest and dividend revenue and
other.

     Management and advisory fees and incenve fees are accounted for as contracts with customers. Under the guidance for contracts
with customers, an enty is required to (a) idenfy the contract(s) with a customer, (b) idenfy the performance obligaons in the
contract, (c) determine the transacon price, (d) allocate the transacon price to the performance obligaons in the contract, and
(e) recognize revenue when (or as) the enty sasﬁes a performance obligaon. In determining the transacon price, an enty may
include variable consideraon only to the extent that it is probable that a signiﬁcant reversal in the amount of cumulave revenue
recognized would not occur when the uncertainty associated with the variable consideraon is resolved. See Note 19. “Segment
Reporng” for a disaggregated presentaon of revenues from contracts with customers.

   Management and Advisory Fees, Net — Management and Advisory Fees, Net are comprised of management fees, including base
management fees, transacon, advisory and other fees net of management fee reducons and oﬀsets.

    Blackstone earns base management fees from its customers at a ﬁxed percentage of a calculaon base which is typically net asset
value, gross asset value, total fair value of investments, commied capital, total invested capital or remaining invested capital. Blackstone
idenﬁes its customers on a fund by fund basis in accordance with the terms and circumstances of the individual fund. Generally the
customer is idenﬁed as the investors in its managed funds and investment vehicles, but for certain widely held funds or vehicles, the
fund or vehicle itself may be idenﬁed as the customer. These customer contracts require Blackstone to provide investment management
services, which represents a performance obligaon that Blackstone sasﬁes over me. Management fees are a form of variable
consideraon because the fees Blackstone is entled to vary based on ﬂuctuaons in the basis for the management fee. The amount
recorded as revenue is generally determined at the end of the period because these management fees are payable on a regular basis
(typically quarterly) and are not subject to clawback once paid.

    Transacon, advisory and other fees are principally fees charged to the investors of funds indirectly through the managed funds and
porolio companies. The investment advisory agreements generally require that the investment adviser reduce the amount of
management fees payable by the investors to Blackstone (“management fee reducons”) by an amount equal to a poron of the
transacon and other fees paid to Blackstone by the porolio companies. The amount of the reducon varies by fund, the type of fee
paid by the porolio company and the previously incurred expenses of the fund. These fees and associated management fee reducons
are a component of the transacon price for Blackstone’s performance obligaon to provide investment management services to the
investors of funds and are recognized as changes to the transacon price in the period in which they are charged and the services are
performed.

    Management fee oﬀsets are reducons to management fees payable by the investors of the Blackstone Funds, which includes
amounts such investors reimburse the Blackstone Funds or Blackstone primarily for placement fees, rebates and other consideraon
determined to be an adjustment to the transacon price. Providing investment management services requires Blackstone to arrange for
services on behalf of its customers. In those situaons where Blackstone is acng as an agent on behalf of the investors of funds, it
presents the cost of services as net against management fee revenue. In all other situaons, Blackstone is primarily responsible for
fulﬁlling the services and is therefore acng as a principal for those arrangements. As a result, the cost of those services is presented as
Compensaon or General, Administrave and Other expense, as appropriate, with any reimbursement from the investors of the funds
recorded as Management and Advisory Fees, Net. In cases where the investors of the funds are determined to be the customer in an
arrangement, placement fees may be capitalized as a cost to acquire a customer contract. Capitalized placement fees are amorzed over
the life of the customer contract, are recorded within Other Assets in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condion and
amorzaon is recorded within General, Administrave and Other within the Consolidated Statements of Operaons. In cases where the
Blackstone Funds are determined to be the customer in the arrangement, placement fees are generally expensed as incurred. Blackstone
may also pay ongoing investor servicing fees to certain distributors of its products. Where Blackstone is the principal in those
arrangements, ongoing investor servicing fees are expensed as incurred and are recorded within General, Administrave and Other
expense.

    Accrued but unpaid Management and Advisory Fees, net of management fee reducons and management fee oﬀsets, as of the
reporng date are included in Due from Aﬃliates in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condion.

     Incenve Fees — Contractual fees earned based on the performance of Blackstone vehicles (“Incenve Fees”) are a form of variable
consideraon in Blackstone’s contracts with customers to provide investment management services. Incenve Fees are earned based on
performance of the vehicle during the period, subject to the achievement of minimum return levels, or high water marks, in accordance
with the respecve terms set out in each vehicle’s governing agreements. Incenve Fees will not be recognized as revenue unl (a) it is
probable that a signiﬁcant reversal in the amount of cumulave revenue recognized will not occur, or (b) the uncertainty associated with
the variable consideraon is subsequently resolved. Incenve Fees are typically recognized as revenue when realized at the end of the
measurement period. Once realized, such fees are not subject to clawback or reversal. Accrued but unpaid Incenve Fees charged directly
to investors in Blackstone vehicles as of the reporng date are recorded within Due from Aﬃliates in the Consolidated Statements of
Financial Condion.

    Investment Income (Loss) — Investment Income (Loss) represents the unrealized and realized gains and losses on Blackstone’s
Performance Allocaons and Principal Investments.

     In carry fund structures and certain open-ended structures, Blackstone, through its subsidiaries, invests alongside its limited partners
in a partnership and is entled to its pro-rata share of the results of the fund vehicle (a “pro-rata allocaon”). In addion to a pro-rata
allocaon, and assuming certain investment returns are achieved, Blackstone is entled to a disproporonate allocaon of the income
otherwise allocable to the limited partners, commonly referred to as carried interest (“Performance Allocaons”).

      Performance Allocaons are made to the general partner based either on cumulave fund performance to date, subject to a
preferred return to limited partners or based on vehicle performance over a period of me, subject to a high water mark and preferred
return to investors. At the end of each reporng period, Blackstone calculates the balance of accrued Performance Allocaons (“Accrued
Performance Allocaons”) that would be due to Blackstone for each fund, pursuant to the fund agreements, as if the fair value of the
underlying investments were realized as of such date, irrespecve of whether such amounts have been realized. As the fair value of
underlying investments varies between reporng periods, it is necessary to make adjustments to amounts recorded as Accrued
Performance Allocaons to reﬂect either (a) posive performance resulng in an increase in the Accrued Performance Allocaon to the
general partner or (b) negave performance that would cause the amount due to Blackstone to be less than the amount previously
recognized as revenue, resulng in a negave adjustment to the Accrued Performance Allocaon to the general partner. In each scenario,
it is necessary to calculate the Accrued Performance Allocaon on cumulave results compared to the Accrued Performance Allocaon
recorded to date and make the required posive or negave adjustments. Blackstone ceases to record negave Performance Allocaons
once previously Accrued Performance Allocaons for such fund have been fully reversed. Blackstone is not obligated to pay guaranteed
returns or hurdles, and therefore, cannot have negave Performance Allocaons over the life of a fund. Accrued Performance Allocaons
as of the reporng date are reﬂected in Investments in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condion.

     Performance Allocaons in carry fund structures are realized when an underlying investment is proﬁtably disposed of and the fund’s
cumulave returns are in excess of the preferred return or, in limited instances, a er certain thresholds for return of capital are met.
Performance Allocaons in carry fund structures are subject to clawback to the extent that the Performance Allocaon received to date
exceeds the amount due to Blackstone based on cumulave results. As such, the accrual for potenal repayment of previously received
Performance Allocaons, which is a component of Due to Aﬃliates, represents all amounts previously distributed to Blackstone Holdings
and non-controlling interest holders that would need to be repaid to the Blackstone carry funds if the Blackstone carry funds were to be
liquidated based on the current fair value of the underlying funds’ investments as of the reporng date. The actual clawback liability,
however, generally does not become realized unl the end of a fund’s life except for certain funds, which may have an interim clawback
liability. Performance Allocaons in open-ended structures are realized based on the stated me period in the agreements and are
generally not subject to clawback once paid.

     Principal Investments include the unrealized and realized gains and losses on Blackstone’s principal investments, including its
investments in Blackstone Funds that are not consolidated and receive pro-rata allocaons, its equity method investments, and other
principal investments. Income (Loss) on Principal Investments is realized when Blackstone redeems all or a poron of its investment or
when Blackstone receives cash income, such as dividends or distribuons. Unrealized Income (Loss) on Principal Investments results from
changes in the fair value of the underlying investment as well as the reversal of unrealized gain (loss) at the me an investment is
realized.

    Interest and Dividend Revenue — Interest consists primarily of interest income earned on cash, receivables and Blackstone held

   Other Revenue — Other Revenue consists of miscellaneous income and foreign exchange gains and losses arising on transacons

Fair Value of Financial Instruments

     GAAP establishes a hierarchical disclosure framework which priorizes and ranks the level of market price observability used in
measuring ﬁnancial instruments at fair value. Market price observability is aﬀected by a number of factors, including the type of ﬁnancial
instrument, the characteriscs speciﬁc to the ﬁnancial instrument and the state of the marketplace, including the existence and
transparency of transacons between market parcipants. Financial instruments with readily available quoted prices in acve markets
generally will have a higher degree of market price observability and a lesser degree of judgment used in measuring fair value.

    Financial instruments measured and reported at fair value are classiﬁed and disclosed based on the observability of inputs used in
the determinaon of fair values, as follows:

    •      Level I — Quoted prices are available in acve markets for idencal ﬁnancial instruments as of the reporng date. The types of
           ﬁnancial instruments in Level I include listed equies, listed derivaves and mutual funds with quoted prices. Blackstone does
           not adjust the quoted price for these investments, even in situaons where Blackstone holds a large posion and a sale could
           reasonably impact the quoted price.
    •      Level II — Pricing inputs are other than quoted prices in acve markets, which are either directly or indirectly observable as of
           the reporng date, and fair value is determined through the use of models or other valuaon methodologies. Financial
           instruments which are generally included in this category include corporate bonds and loans, including corporate bonds and
           loans held within consolidated collateralized loan obligaons (“CLO”) vehicles, government and agency securies, less liquid
           and restricted equity securies, and certain over-the-counter derivaves where the fair value is based on observable inputs.
           Notes issued by consolidated CLO vehicles are classiﬁed within Level II of the fair value hierarchy.
    •      Level III — Pricing inputs are unobservable for the ﬁnancial instruments and includes situaons where there is lile, if any,
           market acvity for the ﬁnancial instrument. The inputs into the determinaon of fair value require signiﬁcant management
           judgment or esmaon. Financial instruments that are included in this category generally include private investments in the
           equity of operang companies, real estate properes, distressed debt and non-investment grade residual interests in
           securizaons, investments in non-consolidated CLOs and certain over-the-counter derivaves where the fair value is based
           on unobservable inputs. For certain investments where the fair value is not readily determinable, net asset value (“NAV”) is
           applied as a praccal expedient.

    In certain cases, the inputs used to measure fair value may fall into diﬀerent levels of the fair value hierarchy. In such cases, the
determinaon of which category within the fair value hierarchy is appropriate for any given ﬁnancial instrument is based on the lowest
level of input that is signiﬁcant to the fair value measurement. Blackstone’s assessment of the signiﬁcance of a parcular input to the fair
value measurement in its enrety requires judgment and considers factors speciﬁc to the ﬁnancial instrument.

Level II Valuaon Techniques

    Financial instruments classiﬁed within Level II of the fair value hierarchy comprise debt instruments, debt securies sold, not yet
purchased and certain equity securies and derivave instruments valued using observable inputs.

    The valuaon techniques used to value ﬁnancial instruments classiﬁed within Level II of the fair value hierarchy are as follows:

    •      Debt Instruments and Equity Securies are valued on the basis of prices from an orderly transacon between market
           parcipants including those provided by reputable dealers or pricing services. In determining the value of a parcular
           investment, pricing services may use certain informaon with respect to transacons in such investments, quotaons from
           dealers, pricing matrices and market transacons in comparable investments and various relaonships between investments.
           The valuaon of certain equity securies is based on an observable price for an idencal security adjusted for the eﬀect of a
           restricon.
    •      Freestanding Derivaves are valued using contractual cash ﬂows and observable inputs comprising yield curves, foreign
           currency rates and credit spreads.
    •      Notes issued by consolidated CLO vehicles are measured based on the more observable fair value of CLO assets less (a) the fair
           value of any beneﬁcial interests held by Blackstone, and (b) the carrying value of any beneﬁcial interests that represent
           compensaon for services.

Level III Valuaon Techniques

    In the absence of observable market prices, Blackstone values its investments using valuaon methodologies applied on a consistent
basis. For some investments lile market acvity may exist; management’s determinaon of fair value is then based on the best
informaon available in the circumstances, and may incorporate management’s own assumpons and involves a signiﬁcant degree of
judgment, taking into consideraon a combinaon of internal and external factors, including the appropriate risk adjustments for
non-performance and liquidity risks. Investments for which market prices are not observable include private investments in the equity of
operang companies, real estate properes and investments in non-consolidated CLO vehicles.

     Real Estate Investments — The fair values of real estate investments are determined by considering projected operang cash ﬂows,
sales of comparable assets, if any, and replacement costs, among other measures and consideraons. The methods used to esmate the
fair value of real estate investments include the discounted cash ﬂow method, where value is calculated by discounng the esmated
cash ﬂows and the esmated terminal value of the subject investment by the assumed buyer’s weighted-average cost of capital. A
terminal value is derived by reference to an exit mulple, such as for esmates of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciaon and
amorzaon (“EBITDA”), or a capitalizaon rate, such as for esmates of net operang income (“NOI”). Valuaons may also be derived by
the performance mulple or market approach, by reference to observable valuaon measures for comparable companies or assets (for
example, dividing NOI by a relevant capitalizaon rate observed for comparable companies or transacons), adjusted by management for
diﬀerences between the investment and the referenced comparables.

     Private Equity Investments — The fair values of private equity investments are determined by reference to projected net earnings,
EBITDA, public market or private transacons, valuaons for comparable companies and other measures which, in many cases, are based
on unaudited informaon at the me received. The methods used to esmate the fair value of private equity investments include the
discounted cash ﬂow method. Where a discounted cash ﬂow method is used, a terminal value is derived by reference to EBITDA or
price/earnings exit mulples. Valuaons may also be derived by reference to observable valuaon measures for comparable companies
or transacons (for example, mulplying a key performance metric of the investee company, such as EBITDA, by a relevant valuaon
mulple observed in the range of comparable companies or transacons), adjusted by management for diﬀerences between the
investment and the referenced comparables, and in some instances by reference to opon pricing models or other similar methods.

    Credit-Focused Investments — The fair values of credit-focused investments are generally determined on the basis of prices between
market parcipants provided by reputable dealers or pricing services. For credit-focused investments that are not publicly traded or
whose market prices are not readily available, Blackstone may ulize other valuaon techniques, including the discounted cash ﬂow
method or a market approach. The discounted cash ﬂow method projects the expected cash ﬂows of the debt instrument based on
contractual terms, and discounts such cash ﬂows back to the valuaon date using a market-based yield. The market-based yield is
generally esmated using yields of publicly traded debt instruments issued by companies operang in similar industries as the subject
investment or based on changes in credit spreads of a broader benchmark index applicable to a subject investment.

    The market approach is generally used to determine the enterprise value of the issuer of a credit investment, and considers valuaon
mulples of comparable companies or transacons. The resulng enterprise value will dictate whether or not such credit investment has
adequate enterprise value coverage. In cases of distressed credit instruments, the market approach may be used to esmate a recovery
value in the event of a restructuring.

Investments, at Fair Value

    Generally, the Blackstone Funds are accounted for as investment companies in accordance with the GAAP guidance on investment
companies, and under the American Instute of Cerﬁed Public Accountants Audit and Accounng Guide, Investment Companies, and
reﬂect their investments, including majority-owned and controlled investments, at fair value. Such consolidated funds’ investments are
reﬂected in Investments on the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condion at fair value, with unrealized gains and losses resulng
from changes in fair value reﬂected as a component of Net Gains (Losses) from Fund Investment Acvies in the Consolidated Statements
of Operaons. Fair value is the amount that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability, in an orderly transacon
between market parcipants at the measurement date, at current market condions (i.e., the exit price).

    Certain principal investments are presented at fair value with unrealized appreciaon or depreciaon and realized gains and losses
recognized in the Consolidated Statements of Operaons within Investment Income (Loss).

    For certain instruments, Blackstone has elected the fair value opon. Such elecon is irrevocable and is applied on an investment by
investment basis at inial recognion or other eligible elecon dates. Blackstone has applied the fair value opon for certain loans and
receivables, unfunded loan commitments and certain investments that otherwise would not have been carried at fair value with gains
and losses recorded in net income. The methodology for measuring the fair value of such investments is consistent with the methodology
applied to private equity, real estate and credit-focused investments. Changes in the fair value of such instruments are recognized in
Investment Income (Loss) in the Consolidated Statements of Operaons. Interest income on interest bearing loans and receivables and
debt securies on which the fair value opon has been elected is based on stated coupon rates adjusted for the accreon of purchase
discounts and the amorzaon of purchase premiums. This interest income is recorded within Interest and Dividend Revenue.

    Blackstone has elected the fair value opon for the assets of consolidated CLO vehicles. As permied under GAAP, Blackstone
measures notes issued by consolidated CLO vehicles as (a) the sum of the fair value of the consolidated CLO assets and the carrying value
of any non-ﬁnancial assets held temporarily, less (b) the sum of the fair value of any beneﬁcial interests retained by Blackstone (other
than those that represent compensaon for services) and Blackstone’s carrying value of any beneﬁcial interests that represent
compensaon for services. As a result of this measurement alternave, there is no aribuon of amounts to Non-Controlling Interests for
consolidated CLO vehicles. Assets of the consolidated CLOs are presented within Investments within the Consolidated Statements of
Financial Condion and notes payable within Loans Payable for the amounts due to unaﬃliated third pares. Changes in the fair value of
consolidated CLO assets and liabilies and related interest, dividend and other income are presented within Net Gains (Losses) from Fund
Investment Acvies. Expenses of consolidated CLO vehicles are presented in Fund Expenses.

     Blackstone may elect to measure certain proprietary investments in equity securies without readily determinable fair values under

    Certain investments of Blackstone and the consolidated Blackstone funds are valued at NAV per share pursuant to the praccal
expedient. In limited circumstances, Blackstone may determine, based on its own due diligence and investment procedures, that NAV per
share does not represent fair value. In such circumstances, Blackstone will esmate the fair value in good faith and in a manner that it

    The terms of the investee’s investment generally provide for minimum holding periods or lock-ups, the instuon of gates on

and as a result, investments may not be redeemable at, or within three months of, the reporng date.

    Security and loan transacons are recorded on a trade date basis.

Equity Method Investments

    Investments in which Blackstone is deemed to exert signiﬁcant inﬂuence, but not control, are accounted for using the equity method
of accounng except in cases where the fair value opon has been elected. Blackstone has signiﬁcant inﬂuence over all Blackstone Funds
in which it invests but does not consolidate. Therefore, its investments in such Blackstone Funds, which generally include both a
proporonate and disproporonate allocaon of the proﬁts and losses (as is the case with funds that include a Performance Allocaon),
are accounted for under the equity method. Under the equity method of accounng, Blackstone’s share of earnings (losses) from equity
method investments is included in Investment Income (Loss) in the Consolidated Statements of Operaons.

     In cases where Blackstone’s equity method investments provide for a disproporonate allocaon of the proﬁts and losses (as is the
case with funds that include a Performance Allocaon), Blackstone’s share of earnings (losses) from equity method investments is
determined using a balance sheet approach referred to as the hypothecal liquidaon at book value (“HLBV”) method. Under the HLBV
method, at the end of each reporng period, Blackstone calculates the Accrued Performance Allocaons that would be due to Blackstone
for each fund pursuant to the fund agreements as if the fair value of the underlying investments were realized as of such date,
irrespecve of whether such amounts have been realized. As the fair value of underlying investments varies between reporng periods, it
is necessary to make adjustments to amounts recorded as Accrued Performance Allocaons to reﬂect either (a) posive performance
resulng in an increase in the Accrued Performance Allocaon to the general partner, or (b) negave performance that would cause the
amount due to Blackstone to be less than the amount previously recognized as revenue, resulng in a negave adjustment to the
Accrued Performance Allocaon to the general partner. In each scenario, it is necessary to calculate the Accrued Performance Allocaon
on cumulave results compared to the Accrued Performance Allocaon recorded to date and make the required posive or negave
adjustments. Blackstone ceases to record negave Performance Allocaons once previously Accrued Performance Allocaons for such
fund have been fully reversed. Blackstone is not obligated to pay guaranteed returns or hurdles, and therefore, cannot have negave
Performance Allocaons over the life of a fund. The carrying amounts of equity method investments are reﬂected in Investments in the
Consolidated Statements of Financial Condion.

     Strategic Partners’ results presented in Blackstone’s consolidated ﬁnancial statements are reported on a three-month lag from
Strategic Partners’ fund ﬁnancial statements, which report the performance of underlying investments generally on a same quarter basis,
if available. Therefore, Strategic Partners’ results presented herein do not reﬂect the impact of economic and market acvity in the
current quarter. Current quarter market acvity of Strategic Partners’ underlying investments is expected to aﬀect Blackstone’s reported
results in upcoming periods.

Income Taxes

     Blackstone Inc. is a corporaon for U.S. federal income tax purposes and thus is subject to U.S. federal, state and local income taxes
on Blackstone’s share of taxable income. The Blackstone Holdings Partnerships and certain of their subsidiaries operate in the U.S. as
partnerships for U.S. federal income tax purposes and generally as corporate enes in non-U.S. jurisdicons. Accordingly, these enes
in some cases are subject to New York City unincorporated business taxes or non-U.S. income taxes. In addion, certain of the wholly
owned subsidiaries of Blackstone and the Blackstone Holdings Partnerships will be subject to federal, state and local corporate income
taxes at the enty level and the related tax provision aributable to Blackstone’s share of this income tax is reﬂected in the consolidated
ﬁnancial statements. Cash paid for transferrable tax credits is reﬂected in Payments for Income Taxes in the Consolidated Statements of
Cash Flows.

Provision for Income Taxes

    Income taxes are provided for using the asset and liability method under which deferred tax assets and liabilies are recognized for
temporary diﬀerences between the ﬁnancial reporng and tax bases of assets and liabilies, resulng in all pretax amounts being
appropriately tax eﬀected in the period, irrespecve of which tax return year items will be reﬂected. Blackstone reports interest expense
and tax penales related to income tax maers in provision for income taxes.

Deferred Income Taxes

     Deferred income taxes reﬂect the net tax eﬀects of temporary diﬀerences between the ﬁnancial reporng and tax bases of assets and
liabilies. These temporary diﬀerences result in taxable or deducble amounts in future years and are measured using the tax rates and
laws that will be in eﬀect when such diﬀerences are expected to reverse. Valuaon allowances are established to reduce the deferred tax
assets to the amount that is more likely than not to be realized. Deferred tax assets are separately stated, and deferred tax liabilies are
included in Accounts Payable, Accrued Expenses, and Other Liabilies in the consolidated ﬁnancial statements.

Reverse Repurchase and Repurchase Agreements

event of a counterparty default, the right to liquidate collateral and the right to oﬀset a counterparty’s rights and obligaons.

    Blackstone takes possession of securies purchased under reverse repurchase agreements and is permied to repledge, deliver or
otherwise use such securies. Blackstone also pledges its ﬁnancial instruments to counterpares to collateralize repurchase agreements.

Consolidated Statements of Financial Condion. Addional disclosures relang to repurchase agreements are included in Note 9.
“Repurchase Agreements.”

    Blackstone does not oﬀset assets and liabilies relang to reverse repurchase agreements and repurchase agreements in its

     For freestanding derivave contracts, Blackstone presents changes in fair value in current period earnings. Changes in the fair value of

5. Derivave Financial Instruments

     Blackstone and the consolidated Blackstone Funds enter into derivave contracts in the normal course of business to achieve certain
risk management objecves and for general investment and business purposes. Blackstone may enter into derivave contracts in order to
hedge its interest rate risk exposure against the eﬀects of interest rate changes. Addionally, Blackstone may also enter into derivave
contracts in order to hedge its foreign currency risk exposure against the eﬀects of a poron of its non-U.S. dollar denominated currency
net investments. As a result of the use of derivave contracts, Blackstone and the consolidated Blackstone Funds are exposed to the risk
that counterpares will fail to fulﬁll their contractual obligaons. To migate such counterparty risk, Blackstone and the consolidated
Blackstone Funds enter into contracts with certain major ﬁnancial instuons, all of which have investment grade rangs. Counterparty
credit risk is evaluated in determining the fair value of derivave instruments.

Freestanding Derivaves

     Freestanding derivaves are instruments that Blackstone and certain of the consolidated Blackstone Funds have entered into as part
of their overall risk management and investment strategies. These derivave contracts are not designated as hedging instruments for
accounng purposes. Such contracts may include interest rate swaps, foreign exchange contracts, equity swaps, opons, futures and
other derivave contracts.

         months of, the reporng date. Investments represenng 1% of fair value of the investments in this category are in liquidaon.
    (2) The Real Estate category includes investments in funds that primarily invest in real estate assets. All investments in this category
         are redeemable as of the reporng date.
    (3) The Infrastructure category includes investments in funds that primarily invest in infrastructure assets and companies. All
         investments in this category may not be redeemed at, or within three months of, the reporng date.
    (4) The Credit Driven category includes investments in hedge funds that invest primarily in domesc and internaonal bonds. All
         investments in these categories may not be redeemed at, or within three months of, the reporng date.
(b) Equity Securies, Partnership and LLC Interest includes investments in investment funds.

8. Variable Interest Enes

     Pursuant to GAAP consolidaon guidance, Blackstone consolidates certain VIEs for which it is the primary beneﬁciary either directly
or indirectly, through a consolidated enty or aﬃliate. VIEs include certain private equity, real estate, credit-focused or funds of hedge
funds enes and CLO vehicles. The purpose of such VIEs is to provide strategy speciﬁc investment opportunies for investors in
exchange for management and performance-based fees. The investment strategies of the Blackstone Funds diﬀer by product; however,
the fundamental risks of the Blackstone Funds are similar, including loss of invested capital and loss of management fees and
performance-based fees. In Blackstone’s role as general partner, collateral manager or investment adviser, it generally considers itself the
sponsor of the applicable Blackstone Fund. Blackstone does not provide performance guarantees and has no other ﬁnancial obligaon to
provide funding to consolidated VIEs other than its own capital commitments.

    The assets of consolidated variable interest enes may only be used to sele obligaons of these enes. In addion, there is no
recourse to Blackstone for the consolidated VIEs’ liabilies.

    Blackstone holds variable interests in certain VIEs which are not consolidated as it is determined that Blackstone is not the primary
beneﬁciary. Blackstone’s involvement with such enes is in the form of direct and indirect equity interests and fee arrangements. The
maximum exposure to loss represents the loss of assets recognized by Blackstone relang to non-consolidated VIEs and any clawback
obligaon relang to previously distributed Performance Allocaons. Blackstone’s maximum exposure to loss relang to non-consolidated
VIEs was as follows:

Noonal Pooling Arrangements

    Blackstone has noonal cash pooling arrangements with ﬁnancial instuons for cash management purposes. These arrangements
allow for cash withdrawals based upon aggregate cash balances on deposit at the same ﬁnancial instuon. Cash withdrawals cannot
exceed aggregate cash balances on deposit. The net balance of cash on deposit and overdra s is used as a basis for calculang net
interest expense or income. As of December 31, 2025, the aggregate cash balance on deposit relang to the cash pooling arrangements
was $781.0 million, which was oﬀset and reported net of the accompanying overdra of $780.9 million.

12. Borrowings

    On October 16, 2025, Blackstone Holdings Finance Co. L.L.C., as borrower, and Blackstone Holdings AI L.P., Blackstone Holdings I L.P.,
Blackstone Holdings II L.P., Blackstone Holdings III L.P. and Blackstone Holdings IV L.P., as guarantors, entered into an amended and
restated $4.325 billion revolving credit facility (the “Revolving Credit Facility”) with Cibank, N.A., as administrave agent, and the
lenders party thereto. The Revolving Credit Facility amends and restates Blackstone’s exisng revolving credit facility to, among other
things, extend the maturity date from December 15, 2028 to October 16, 2030 and increase the aggregate required minimum amount of
fee generang assets under management.

    On November 3, 2025, Blackstone, through its subsidiary Blackstone Reg Finance Co. L.L.C., issued $600 million aggregate principal
amount of senior notes due November 3, 2030 (the “Registered 2030 Notes”), and $600 million aggregate principal amount of senior
notes due February 15, 2036 (the “Registered 2036 Notes” and, together with the Registered 2030 Notes, the “Registered Notes”),
pursuant to a Registraon Statement on Form S-3. The Registered 2030 Notes have an interest rate of 4.300% per annum, and the
Registered 2036 Notes have an interest rate of 4.950%. The Registered Notes accrue interest from November 3, 2025. Interest on the
Registered 2030 Notes is payable semi-annually in arrears on May 3 and November 3 of each year commencing on May 3, 2026. Interest
on the Registered 2036 Notes is payable semi-annually in arrears on February 15 and August 15 of each year commencing on
February 15, 2026.

Tax Receivable Agreements

     Blackstone used a poron of the proceeds from the IPO and other sales of shares to purchase interests in the predecessor businesses
from the predecessor owners. In addion, holders of Blackstone Holdings Partnership Units may exchange their Blackstone Holdings
Partnership Units for shares of Blackstone common stock on a one-for-one basis. The purchase and subsequent exchanges are expected
to result in increases in the tax basis of the tangible and intangible assets of Blackstone Holdings and therefore reduce the amount of tax
that Blackstone would otherwise be required to pay in the future.

     Blackstone has entered into tax receivable agreements with each of the predecessor owners. In addion, others who acquire
Blackstone Holdings Partnership Units, including senior managing directors, execute tax receivable agreements. The agreements provide
for the payment by the corporate taxpayer to such owners of 85% of the amount of cash savings, if any, in U.S. federal, state and local
income tax that the corporate taxpayers actually realize as a result of the aforemenoned increases in tax basis and of certain other tax
beneﬁts related to entering into these tax receivable agreements. For purposes of the tax receivable agreements, cash savings in income
tax will be computed by comparing the actual income tax liability of the corporate taxpayers to the amount of such taxes that the
corporate taxpayers would have been required to pay had there been no increase to the tax basis of the tangible and intangible assets of
Blackstone Holdings as a result of the exchanges and had the corporate taxpayers not entered into the tax receivable agreements.

     Assuming no future material changes in the relevant tax law and that the corporate taxpayers earn suﬃcient taxable income to
realize the full tax beneﬁt of the increased amorzaon of the assets, the expected future payments under the tax receivable agreements
(which are taxable to the recipients) will aggregate $2.1 billion over the next 15 years. The a er-tax net present value of these esmated
payments totals $699.3 million assuming a 15% discount rate and using Blackstone’s most recent projecons relang to the esmated
ming of the beneﬁt to be received. Future payments under the tax receivable agreements in respect of subsequent exchanges would be
in addion to these amounts. The payments under the tax receivable agreements are not condioned upon connued ownership of
Blackstone equity interests by the pre-IPO owners and the others menoned above. Subsequent to December 31, 2025, payments
totaling $70.6 million were made to certain pre-IPO owners and others menoned above in accordance with the tax receivable
agreement and related to tax beneﬁts Blackstone received for the 2024 taxable year.

    Amounts related to the deferred tax asset resulng from the increase in tax basis from the exchange of Blackstone Holdings
Partnership Units to shares of Blackstone common stock, the resulng remeasurement of net deferred tax assets at the Blackstone
ownership percentage at the date of the Consolidated Statement of Financial Condion, the due to aﬃliates for the future payments
resulng from the tax receivable agreements and resulng adjustment to partners’ capital are included as Deferred Tax Asset Eﬀects from
Equity Transacons in the Supplemental Disclosure of Non-Cash Invesng and Financing Acvies in the Consolidated Statements of Cash
Flows.

BREIT as of the subscripon dates, including any appreciaon or dividends received by Blackstone in respect thereof. Pursuant to the UC
strategic ventures, Blackstone is entled to receive an incremental 5% cash payment from UC Investments on any returns received in

investment of €1.0 billion in a vehicle managed in the Real Estate segment. The long-term strategic venture provides for a target return of
9.25% supported by a pledge by Blackstone of €200 million of its holdings in a related vehicle.

    Blackstone may from me to me be involved in ligaon and claims incidental to the conduct of its business. Blackstone’s

     Blackstone accrues a liability for legal proceedings only when those maers present loss conngencies that are both probable and

     In December 2017, eight pension plan members of the Kentucky Rerement System (“KRS”) ﬁled a derivave lawsuit on behalf of KRS
in Franklin County Circuit Court in Kentucky (the “Mayberry Acon”). Plainﬀs alleged breaches of ﬁduciary duty and other violaons of
Kentucky law in connecon with KRS’s investment in three hedge funds of funds, including a fund managed by Blackstone Alternave
Asset Management L.P. (“BLP”). The suit named more than 30 defendants, including, among others, The Blackstone Group L.P. (now
Blackstone Inc.); BLP; Stephen A. Schwarzman, as Chairman and CEO of Blackstone; and J. Tomilson Hill, as then-CEO of BLP (collecvely,
the “Blackstone Defendants”). In July 2020, the Kentucky Supreme Court directed the Circuit Court to dismiss the acon for lack of
standing.

   In July 2020, the Kentucky Aorney General (the “AG”) ﬁled its own acon asserng substanally idencal claims against largely the
same defendants (the “July 2020 Acon”). In May 2024, the Court denied the Blackstone Defendants’ and most other defendants’
moons to dismiss the July 2020 Acon. In April 2024, the AG amended its complaint, adding breach-of-contract claims against the fund
manager defendants. Defendants moved to dismiss this amended complaint in June 2024. Those moons are pending.

    In August 2022, KRS was ordered to disclose a 2021 report it commissioned to invesgate the investment acvies underlying the
lawsuit. The report “did not ﬁnd any violaons of ﬁduciary duty or illegal acvity by [BLP],” and quotes communicaons by KRS staﬀ
during the period of the investment recognizing that BLP was exceeding KRS’s returns benchmark, providing KRS with “far fewer negave
months than any liquid market comparable,” and that BLP “[h]as killed it.”

    In January 2021, certain former plainﬀs in the Mayberry Acon ﬁled a separate acon (“Taylor I”) against the Blackstone Defendants
and other defendants in the Mayberry Acon, asserng substanally similar allegaons as the AG’s July 2020 acon did, but styled as a
direct class acon. Taylor I was removed to the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Kentucky and stayed pending the outcome of
the AG’s July 2020 acon.

      In August 2021, a group of KRS members—including those that ﬁled Taylor I—ﬁled an acon in Franklin County Circuit Court (“Taylor
II”) substanally similar to Taylor I, against the Blackstone Defendants, other defendants named in the Mayberry Acon, and other KRS
oﬃcials. The Court denied most defendants’ moons to dismiss this acon in May 2024. The Blackstone Defendants and the other fund
manager defendants ﬁled a peon for a writ of prohibion from that denial. In November 2024, the Kentucky Court of Appeals denied

Conngent Obligaons (Clawback)

    Performance Allocaons are subject to clawback to the extent that the Performance Allocaons received to date with respect to a
fund exceeds the amount due to Blackstone based on cumulave results of that fund. The actual clawback liability, however, generally
does not become realized unl the end of a fund’s life except for certain Blackstone funds, which may have an interim clawback liability.
The lives of the funds, including available contemplated extensions, for which a liability for potenal clawback obligaons has been
recorded for ﬁnancial reporng purposes, are currently ancipated to expire at various points through 2038. Further extensions of such
terms may be implemented under given circumstances.

     For ﬁnancial reporng purposes, when applicable, the general partners record a liability for potenal clawback obligaons to the
limited partners of some of the funds due to changes in the unrealized value of a fund’s remaining investments and where the fund’s
general partner has previously received Performance Allocaon distribuons with respect to such fund’s realized investments. The
liability is based on the general partner’s net obligaon to the fund assuming all remaining investments were realized as of the end of
each reporng period at the fair value of the underlying investments.

(b) Total is a component of Due to Aﬃliates. See Note 17. “Related Party Transacons — Aﬃliate Receivables and Payables — Due to
    Aﬃliates.”

     During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Blackstone general partners paid a cash clawback obligaon of $52.3 million related
to interim and ﬁnal cash clawbacks for funds in the Real Estate, Credit & Insurance and Private Equity segments, of which $31.6 million
was paid by Blackstone Holdings and $20.7 million by current and former Blackstone personnel.

     For Private Equity, Real Estate, and certain Credit & Insurance Funds, a poron of the Performance Allocaons paid to current and
former Blackstone personnel is held in segregated accounts in the event of a cash clawback obligaon. These segregated accounts are not
included in the consolidated ﬁnancial statements of Blackstone, except to the extent a poron of the assets held in the segregated
accounts may be allocated to a consolidated Blackstone fund of hedge funds. At December 31, 2025, $1.2 billion was held in segregated
accounts for the purpose of meeng any clawback obligaons of current and former personnel if such payments are required.

   In the Credit & Insurance segment, payment of Performance Allocaons to Blackstone by the majority of the stressed/distressed,
mezzanine and credit alpha strategies funds are substanally deferred under the terms of the partnership agreements. This deferral
migates the need to hold funds in segregated accounts in the event of a cash clawback obligaon.

    If, at December 31, 2025, all of the investments held by Blackstone’s carry funds were deemed worthless, a possibility that
management views as remote, the amount of Performance Allocaons subject to potenal clawback would be $(8.3) billion, on an
a er-tax basis where applicable, of which Blackstone Holdings is potenally liable for $(7.7) billion if current and former Blackstone
personnel default on their share of the liability, a possibility that management also views as remote.

19. Segment Reporng

    Blackstone conducts its alternave asset management businesses through four segments:

    •      Real Estate – Blackstone’s Real Estate segment primarily comprises its management of opportunisc real estate funds, Core+
           real estate funds, and real estate debt strategies.
    •      Private Equity – Blackstone’s Private Equity segment includes its management of ﬂagship Corporate Private Equity funds,
           sector and geographically-focused Corporate Private Equity funds, core private equity funds, an opportunisc investment
           plaorm, a secondary funds business and GP Stakes, infrastructure-focused funds, a life sciences investment plaorm, a
           growth equity investment plaorm, investment plaorms oﬀering eligible individual investors access to Blackstone’s private
           equity and infrastructure capabilies, a mul-asset investment program for eligible high net worth investors and a capital
           markets services business.

                                                             Blackstone Inc.
